previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia and tracheostomy was admitted for chills, increased dyspnea, and dark green, blood-tinged sputum from her tracheostomy. She had recently been treated for Staphylococcus lugdunensis bacteremia and was on home vancomycin. Evaluation revealed no acute findings on chest X-ray, and ENT found no tracheal inflammation or purulence. Sputum culture grew MRSA, prompting a 5-day course of IV vancomycin at 1000 mg every 12 hours, up from her prior dose due to a low trough. She also received a unit of packed red blood cells for acute on chronic iron deficiency anemia, with hemoglobin improving from 6.8 to 8.2 g/dL. Hemoglobin electrophoresis was pending at discharge. She improved clinically, with resolution of chills and decreased secretions, and was discharged home to complete antibiotics with home health support.

# Question tracheobronchitis, recurrent:  During last 
hospitalization was evaluated by ID, IP, and ENT, who ultimately 
recommended a 5 day course of vancomycin for MRSA in sputum.  
Two days after completing her antibiotic course she redeveloped 
symptoms concerning for recurrent tracheobronchitis (shaking 
chills, increased purulent mucus secretions).  Chest x-ray 
without evidence of pneumonia.  Sputum cultures with rare growth 
commensal flora.  She was started on empiric vancomycin and 
cefepime, but infectious disease team did not feel she was 
acutely infected, and recommended discontinuation of 
antibiotics.  She remained afebrile, respiratory status remained 
stable, despite discontinuation of antibiotics.  
- Interventional pulmonary team evaluated the patient and 
reinforced tracheostomy care as follows:  Portex Thermovent® T2 
heat and moisture exchanger (HME) during the day every day to 
prevent drying up of secretions and predisposition
to tracheobronchitis. At night she was recommended use a trach 
mask w/humidified oxygen and she will need have a new HME every 
day.
